name: TX-19
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+25 partisan lean in a West Texas open seat
Republican Tom Sell's massive financial advantage ($2.1M raised plus $1.3M outside support vs. $31K for the Democrat)
Prediction markets price the Republican at 98%
No polls or expert ratings, but fundamentals are lopsided
model.rationale: This open seat sits in a district that leans 25 points Republican, and the GOP nominee has outraised the Democrat by roughly 70-to-1 with heavy outside backing, while markets give the Democrat about a 1% chance. Nothing in the evidence suggests movement away from the strong fundamentals-based expectation of a wide Republican win.
model.watch: A surprise polling series showing the Democrat within single digits, or a major scandal involving the Republican nominee, would be the first sign this is closer than the lean implies.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Jodey Arrington (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
West Texas's 19th District is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the country, with a partisan lean of about 25 points toward the GOP, and Representative Jodey Arrington's retirement leaves the seat open but does not change its fundamentals. The Republican nominee, Tom Sell, has raised over $2.1 million and benefits from roughly $1.3 million in outside support, while Democrat Kyle Rable has raised about $31,000 with no outside spending on either side.

Prediction markets give the Republican a 98% chance of winning, and no general-election polls or expert ratings exist to complicate the picture. The financial gap, the district's lean, and the open-seat dynamics all point in the same direction, making this a Safe Republican race with a wide expected margin.
